summary.intent: Execute Phase 35 (Phala Testnet TEE Migration) using GSD wave-based execution, but the session pivoted when a major architectural gap was discovered: the TEE worker was duplicating functionality already in shared @cipherbox packages.
summary.outcome: Phase 35 plans were fully restructured from 5 to 6 plans with a new Plan 35-01 (shared package integration + tee-worker move to apps/), all plans renumbered, path-updated, verifier-checked, and committed/pushed to the phase branch.

repo: tee-worker was at repo root, NOT in the pnpm workspace (pnpm-workspace.yaml only covers apps/*, packages/*, tests/*) — it had zero @cipherbox/* dependencies and vendored its own copies of eciesjs, @noble/*, ipns, @libp2p/crypto, multiformats

tee-worker duplicated: ipns-signer.ts vs @cipherbox/core createIpnsRecord(), ECIES ops in key-manager.ts vs @cipherbox/crypto wrapKey/unwrapKey/reWrapKey, provider HTTP code in migration-worker.ts vs @cipherbox/sdk-core KuboProvider/PsaProvider

API instrumentation stack: prom-client for Prometheus, NestJS built-in Logger, HTTP metrics interceptor — metric naming convention is cipherbox_* prefix; API already tracks cipherbox_republish_batch_duration_seconds
@cipherbox/sdk-core KuboProvider and PsaProvider do NOT have injectable fetchFn/timeoutMs — Plan 35-01 must add this injection point before TEE worker can reuse them
apps/api/Dockerfile uses pnpm workspace build pattern — this is the reference Dockerfile pattern for tee-worker's new location at apps/tee-worker/

code.finding: Duplicates @cipherbox/core createIpnsRecord() — same libp2p conversion and marshaling, safe to remove after shared package integration
Duplicates @cipherbox/crypto wrapKey/unwrapKey/reWrapKey — reimplements ECIES wrapping with its own eciesjs import
Contains parallel provider implementations (Kubo/PSA HTTP fetch/pin/unpin) that should be replaced by @cipherbox/sdk-core KuboProvider/PsaProvider
No @cipherbox/* workspace dependencies — standalone package not in pnpm workspace, causing all duplication
Needs fetchFn/timeoutMs injection before TEE worker can reuse it — Plan 35-01 task to add this

workflow: GSD plan verifiers caught real blockers: Dockerfile using npm ci with workspace:* deps would break, Counter() missing new keyword, double path typo @apps/apps/tee-worker/
Wave numbering should start at 1 — GSD executor may not handle wave 0 correctly
When renumbering plans, depends_on references, context paths, key-files paths, and SUMMARY.md output paths all need updating — easy to miss one
Stale STATE.md/config.json changes from a previous interrupted GSD execution need to be discarded before replanning to avoid noise
NestJS was explicitly evaluated and rejected for TEE worker — too many deps (~30+), large attack surface, slow cold start; prom-client directly on Express achieves same observability goals
GSD plan checkers should be run in parallel (spawned 4 simultaneously) rather than sequentially to save time

friction: Phase execution was started and interrupted mid-wave (executor agents partially spawned) before the architectural gap was discovered — required stopping background agents and discarding stale STATE.md changes
Multiple rounds of path updates needed across 6 plan files when renaming tee-worker/ → apps/tee-worker/ — required many individual Edit operations and a final grep scan to catch stragglers
Old 35-02 plan content was overwritten before being renumbered to 35-03, requiring retrieval from git history
35-02 required the most individual Edit operations (~15) due to many scattered tee-worker/ path references
VALIDATION.md had residual 'Wave 0' and 'Wave 1' references that persisted through multiple edit passes
open_items: Plan 35-01 needs to add fetchFn/timeoutMs injection to KuboProvider and PsaProvider in @cipherbox/sdk-core before TEE worker can use them

Plan 35-03 instrumentation: prom-client Counter/Histogram metrics wiring, GET /metrics route, structured JSON logger replacing console.log — deferred to execution
